In addition to any wages herein provided for, the Employer shall contribute into the appropriate Local Promotion Trust the amount specified in the applicable wage provisions of this Agreement for each hour worked for the Employer by those of his employees covered by this Agreement. The Illinois Masonry Institute Promotion Trust shall be administered by five (5) Trustees, of which three (3) shall be appointed by the Mason Contractors Association of Greater Chicago, and two (2) shall be appointed by the Builders Association of Chicago. The Trustees shall be advised by five (5) persons appointed by the Union.
sections.subject: Firm

sections.content: 33.23 Masonry Industry Advancement Fund Contributions:

In addition to any wages herein provided for, the Employer shall contribute into the Masonry Industry Advancement Fund the amount specified in the wage provision of this Agreement for each hour worked for the Employer by those of his employees covered by this Agreement.
sections.subject: Firm

sections.content: 33.24 Annuity Fund Contributions:

The Employer shall contribute for annuity purposes the amount specified in the applicable wage provisions of this Agreement per hour for each hour worked by all employees and supervisors covered by this Agreement. Such payments shall be made to the appropriate Annuity Fund in accordance with the Agreement and Declaration of Trust establishing such Annuity Fund. Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Section 33.24 or elsewhere in this Agreement, contributions to the appropriate Annuity Fund shall include the premium rates included in the wages paid to employees. Thus, if an employee works forty hours at straight time and four hours at time-and-a-half during a given week, that employee will receive the equivalent of forty-six hours' pay and the Annuity Fund contribution on behalf of that employee for the week will also be the equivalent of forty-six hours. Nothing in this provision concerning contributions to the Annuity Fund will affect the manner in which contributions are determined or paid to any fringe benefit fund other than the Annuity Fund.
sections.subject: Firm

sections.content: 33.25 Training Center Fund Contributions:

In addition to any wages herein provided for, the Employer shall contribute into the District Council Training Center Fund the amount specified in the applicable wage provisions of this Agreement for each hour worked for the Employer by those of his employees covered by this Agreement.
sections.subject: Firm

sections.content: 33.26 International Pension Fund Contributions:
In addition to any wages herein provided for, the Employer shall contribute into the Bricklayers and Trowel Trades
International Pension Fund the amount specified in the applicable wage provisions of this Agreement for each hour worked for the Employer by those of his employees covered by this Agreement.
sections.subject: Firm

sections.content: 33.27 Depository Account for Employer Contributions:

A. The amounts contributed pursuant to this Article shall be remitted by the Employer to a Depository Account for Employer Contributions maintained at the Northern Trust Company or at such other banking institution the parties may agree upon in writing from time to time ("Bank") as agent of the Employer for the sole purpose of receiving and distributing contributions to the appropriate funds. All payments shall be made in one check payable to the order of the "Bricklayers Northern Trust Fringe Benefit Account," together with completed remittance forms provided by the Masonry Institute. The Bank shall distribute the contributions in accordance with the terms of this Agreement based on the Standard Payment and instructions given by the Masonry Institute concerning the Home Local, if any, of each employee. The Bank shall have no obligation or responsibility for distributing funds other than based on the Standard Payment.

B. Upon receipt, the Bank shall immediately forward a copy of the Employer's remittance form to the Masonry Institute for processing. A fee not to exceed two percent (2%) of the contributions received shall be deducted by the Bank and forwarded to the Masonry Institute to cover the cost of its administrative and computer services, provided however, that the entire contribution required pursuant to this Agreement shall be deemed to have been paid by the Employer notwithstanding such deduction.
sections.subject: Firm

sections.content: 33.28 Additional Employer Obligation:

The Employer agrees to be bound by the Agreements and Declarations of Trust establishing the Trusts described in this Article, as well as any amendments thereto, and agrees to be bound by all actions taken by the Trustees of said Trusts, pursuant to said Agreements and Declarations of
sections.subject: Firm

sections.content: Trust, except that, in the event of any conflict between the terms of an Agreement and Declaration of Trust and this Agreement, the terms of this Agreement shall control.
Notwithstanding any other provisions to the contrary in this Agreement or in such Agreements and Declarations of Trust, contributions shall be due and payable as provided in this Article.
33.29 Union Cooperation:

Inasmuch as it is anticipated that the existence and utilization of the trust funds described in this Article will result in increased masonry work and, therefore, in increased job opportunities for bricklayers, the Union agrees to cooperate in assuring that contributions required by this Article are in fact made by Employers bound by this Agreement.
sections.subject: Union

sections.content: 33.30 Payment of Contributions and Delinquencies:

A. Contributions must be received by the Bank on or before the twentieth (20) day of each month, covering all employment performed during the preceding month for which contributions are to be paid by the Employer.
sections.subject: Firm

sections.content: B. Any Employer failing to make prompt and timely payment of the contribution to the Health and Welfare Funds, the Pension Funds, the Apprenticeship Programs, the Promotion Trust Funds, the Annuity Funds, the District Council Training Center Fund, or the International Pension Fund in accordance with this Agreement, shall in addition to the storesaid hourly contributions pay each month as liquidated damages for failure to make such timely payment, an additional amount equal to one (1) percent per month on all amounts remaining unpaid (including amounts due as liquidated damages hereunder) as and for liquidated damages for failure to pay in accordance with this Agreement, it being understood and agreed that damages resulting from such late payments are substantial but are difficult if not impossible to ascertain.
sections.subject: Firm

sections.content: C. If delinquency continues uncured for forty-eight

(48) hours after written notice of such delinquency is mailed or delivered to the delinquent Employer, the Employer shall be liable for claims for the extent of benefits to which the employee would have been entitled if the Employer had made the required contributions, and for all contributions and liquidated damages due thereunder, plus all reasonable legal fees incurred by or on behalf of the Health and Welfare Funds, Apprenticeship Programs, Pension Funds, Annuity Funds, Promotion Trust Funds, District Council Training Center Fund, or the International Pension Fund in enforcing the payment thereof.
sections.subject: Firm

sections.content: D. It shall be considered a violation of this Agreement for an Employer to fail to pay or comply with any provisions of this Article or any rule or regulation made by the Trustees administering the Health and Welfare Funds, Apprenticeship Programs, Pension Funds, Promotion Trust Funds, Annuity Funds, District Council Training Center Fund, or International Pension Fund. In the event that the Unions receive written notice from one or more of the Trustees of either the Health and Welfare Funds, Pension Funds, Apprenticeship Programs, Promotion Trust Funds, Annuity Funds, District Council Training Center Fund, or International Pension Fund designated by the Trustees for that purpose, that the Employer has failed to pay in full any sum due the Health and Welfare Funds, Pension Funds, Apprenticeship Programs, Promotion Trust Funds, Annuity Funds, District Council Training Center Fund, or International Pension Fund under this Article and that such failure has continued for forty-eight (48) hours after an Employer has received written notice thereof, the Union is permitted to stop any job of that Employer, and may publicize such stoppage or attempted stoppage of work, until all sums due from the Employer under this Article have been paid in full. This remedy shall be in addition to all other remedies available to the Unions and the Trustees, and may be exercised by the Unions, anything in this collective bargaining agreement to the contrary notwithstanding. Such stoppage or attempted stoppage of work and the publicizing of such to collect contributions to the Health and Welfare Funds, Pension Funds, Apprenticeship Programs, Promotion Trust Funds, Annuity Funds, District Council Training Center Fund, or International Pension Fund.
sections.subject: Union

sections.content: shall not be considered a violation of this Agreement on the part of the Union and it shall not be a subject of arbitration.

E. If employees are withdrawn from any job in order to collect contributions to the Health and Welfare Funds, the Pension Funds, Apprenticeship Programs, Promotion Trust Funds, Annuity Funds, District Council Training Center Fund, or International Pension Fund, the employees who are affected by such stoppage of work shall be paid for lost time up to 16 hours provided that two (2) days' notice of the intention to remove employees from a job is given to the Employer by the Union by registered or certified mall.
sections.subject: Union

sections.content: F. The Employer shall furnish to the Trustees, upon request, such information and reports as they may require in the performance of their duties. The Trustees, or any authorized agent of the Trustees, shall have the right at all reasonable times during business hours to enter upon the premises of the Employer and to examine and copy such books, records, papers, and reports of the Employer as may be necessary to permit the Trustee to determine whether the Employer is fully complying with the provisions regarding Employer contributions. Any Employer found delinquent through regular or special audit ordered by the Trustees shall be charged the full cost of such audit.
sections.subject: Firm

sections.content: G. The Trustees are hereby given the power and the authority to institute whatever legal proceedings may be necessary to enforce compliance with the provisions of this Article. Legal fees incurred by the Trustees in enforcing compliance with this Article shall be charged to the delinquent Employer.
sections.subject: Firm

sections.content: H. The contributions, as aforesaid, shall accrue with respect to all hours worked by any journeyman or apprentice, or supervisor to the extent this Agreement so provides, represented by the Union or for any person doing any work within the jurisdiction of the Union and said contributions shall accrue with respect to all hours worked by employees, and by supervisors to the extent this Agreement so provides, covered by the terms of this Joint Agreement for Employers
sections.subject: Firm

sections.content: within or without the geographical jurisdiction of the Union's jurisdiction, except that when work is performed outside the Union's jurisdiction wherein another Welfare Plan or Pension Plan is effective and the Employer makes contributions to that fund, then the said Employer shall not be required to make a double contribution; provided, however, that the primary duty to make payments for work performed within the jurisdiction of the Union shall be for all Employers to pay to the Health and Welfare Funds, the Pension Funds, the Apprenticeship Programs, the Promotion Trust Funds, the Annuity Funds, the District Council Training Center Fund, and the International Pension Fund, the contributions provided for in this Agreement.
sections.subject: Firm

sections.content: 33.31 Reports to Union and Trustees:

A. In order to assist in the collection of the contributions required pursuant to this Agreement, all Employers shall furnish the following reports to the Trustees of the Health and Welfare Funds, Pension Funds, Apprenticeship Programs, Promotion Trust Funds, Annuity Funds, District Council Training Center Fund, International Pension Fund, or to the Union as indicated:
sections.subject: Firm

sections.content: (1) All Employers shall annually furnish to the Trustees of the Health and Welfare Funds, Pension Funds, Apprenticeship Programs, Promotion Trust Funds, Annuity Funds, District Council Training Center Fund, and International Pension Fund on dates determined by the respective Trustees, a statement showing whether (1) the Employer is a corporation and the names of all officers and directors of said Employer; (2) if not a corporation, a certificate stating who are the constituent persons composing the Employer and their respective Interest in the same.
sections.subject: Firm

sections.content: (2) Each Employer shall furnish to the Bricklayers Northern Trust Fringe Benefit Account, on a monthly basis, a remittance report listing the names of all Bricklayers employed by the Em-
sections.subject: Firm

sections.content: ployer during the month which the remittance report is made. For months in which no Brick-layers were employed, the remittance report of the Employer for that month shall so state. The reports required to be furnished pursuant to this section shall be received by the Bank on or before the twentieth (20th) day of each month.

(3) Each Employer shall furnish to the Union on a weekly basis a report listing the name and address of each job site where work covered by this Agreement was performed during the week for which the report is made and the name of the foreman employed on each job.
sections.subject: Firm

sections.content: B. If any Employer fails to file the required reports provided for above and such failure continues for seventy-two (72) hours after the Employer has received written notice thereof, the Union may stop any job of that Employer and/or withdraw the employees from such Employer's employment and may publicize such stoppage or attempted stoppage of work, until all required reports have been provided, anything in this Agreement to the contrary notwithstanding.
sections.subject: Union

sections.content: 33.32 Payment Bond:

A. Any Employer who is delinquent for sixty (60) days or more in making payments of wages, fringe benefit fund contributions, or any Union dues which have been deducted from the wages of employees pursuant to a check-off authorization shall, at the request of the Union, furnish a satisfactory surety company's bond to guarantee payment of wages and contributions to said funds and Union dues which have been deducted from the wages of an employee pursuant to a check-off authorization as required by this Agreement. The bond shall be in the amount of $5,000.00 if the Employer has three (3) employees or fewer working under this Agreement; in the amount of $15,000.00 if the Employer has four (4) to ten (10) such employees; in the amount of $30,000.00 if the Employer has eleven (11) to twenty (20) such employees; in
sections.subject: Firm

sections.content: the amount of $45,000.00 if the Employer has twenty-one (21) to thirty (30) such employees. The bond shall increase $15,000.00 for each additional ten (10) employees.

The determination of the number of employees working under the Agreement for purposes of setting the amount of the bond will be based on the largest number of such employees within the twelve month period preceding the Union's request that a bond be posted but the Union may, at its sole discretion, request or agree to accept a bond in a lesser amount if the Union determines that a bond in a lesser amount is reasonably likely to provide the security sought and that requiring a bond in a greater amount would present a significant burden to the Employer. No action by the Union in requesting or agreeing to accept a bond in a lesser amount than otherwise provided from one Employer but not from another Employer will be deemed to violate the Most Favored Nations Clause of the Agreement.
sections.subject: Union

sections.content: If an Employer becomes delinquent for sixty (60) days with respect to any of the specified obligations, it is required to post a bond upon request by the Union even if it cures or has cured the delinquency.
sections.subject: Firm

sections.content: The Union may, at its sole discretion, accept a cash bond, irrevocable letter of credit, or other security instrument which it deems proper, and if such an alternate security instrument is provided and accepted, all references in this Article and elsewhere in this Agreement to a "bond" shall be deemed to apply to such alternate security instrument.
sections.subject: Union

sections.content: Any Employer which is required to post a bond pursuant to this section shall maintain the bond until it has satisfied all obligations under the Agreement and has incurred no delinquencies for two years.
sections.subject: Firm

sections.content: B. In the event that a bond is posted, delinquencies occur, recovery is sought against the bond, and the total unpaid wages and benefit fund contributions and Union dues exceed the amount of the bond, payment shall be apportioned among all wages and benefit contributions and Union dues on
a pro rata basis, whereby each wage claim and each fringe benefit obligation and each payment of Union dues will be paid at the same percentage.

C. Notwithstanding anything to the contrary elsewhere in this Agreement, the Union is not required to utilize the grievance or arbitration procedure if an Employer which may be required to post a payment bond fails to do so within ten days of the time the Union submits a written request to the Employer to do so. The Union may, upon expiration of such ten days, seek immediate relief in any court of proper jurisdiction. If the Union utilizes this provision of the Agreement to obtain an order from a court requiring an Employer to furnish a payment bond, the Union shall be entitled to recover from that Employer all reasonable legal fees and cost incurred, and shall be entitled to recover such fees and costs as a part of the legal action without resort to the grievance or arbitration procedure.
sections.subject: Union

sections.content: Notwithstanding anything to the contrary elsewhere in this Agreement, if an Employer which is required to post a payment bond fails to do so within ten days of the time the Union submits a written request to the Employer to do so, the Union may, at its sole discretion, withdraw the employees of the Employer or take other economic action, and may publicize its dispute with the Employer regarding the obligation to post a bond. The Union's rights to engage in such actions and to take other steps as described in this Section to obtain a bond are cumulative. No decision or action by the Union to use one or more methods of seeking to obtain a bond from one Employer but not from another Employer will be deemed to violate the Most Favored Nations Clause of the Agreement.
sections.subject: Union

sections.content: D. If any party to this Agreement believes there is a reasonable possibility that wages, contributions required by this Article, or Union dues which have been deducted from the wages of an employee pursuant to a check-off authorization will go unpaid and will be lost if no action is taken to obtain a payment bond prior to an Employer being delinquent for sixty (60) days or more, that party may, upon 72 hours written notice to such Employer, present the question to the Joint Arbi

tration Board ("JAB") as discussed in Article XII of this Agreement. The JAB will be required to convene and hear evidence presented by the party raising the issue, along with any evidence presented by or on behalf of the Employer in question. If the JAB determines there is a reasonable possibility that the payment of wages, contributions required by this Article, or the Union dues will not be made and will be lost in the absence of such action, it shall require the employer to obtain a payment bond as discussed in Paragraph A of this Section, notwithstanding the fact that no delinquency exists or that a delinquency has not existed for sixty (50) days. In determining whether a payment bond should be required under these circumstances, the JAB cannot act in an arbitrary manner. Without limiting the right of the JAB to require an Employer to obtain a payment bond under the provisions set forth in this paragraph for other reasons, one reason the JAB may require an Employer to obtain such a bond is that the Employer, or an owner or principal of the Employer, is or was associated with or affiliated with an Employer which had delinquencies on previous occasions. If the JAB rules an Employer should obtain a payment bond pursuant to the terms of this paragraph, the Employer must do so within ten days of receipt of written notice of such decision by the JAB and if the Employer falls to do so, the Union may then utilize the procedures set forth in Paragraph C of this section.
sections.subject: Union

sections.content: E. Any employer who signs or becomes bound to this collective bargaining agreement with the Union after May 31, 2000 ("New Employer") will be required within 14 days of signing or becoming bound to the Agreement to post a bond in an amount determined by the number of its employees in accord with the formula set forth in Section 33.32 A. The provisions of Section 33.32 A., B., and C. shall apply to such bonds posted by a New Employer except that (1) in addition to the remedies provided in Section 33.32 C. available to the Union, the Union may also cancel the collective bargaining agreement with the New Employer for failing to comply with the obligation to post a bond, which cancellation will be effective upon the Union giving the New Employer written notice it is exercising this right, and (2) any New Employer who posts such a bond as required and has no delinquencies for two
sections.subject: Firm

sections.content: years from the date of signing or becoming bound to the Agreement shall be permitted to cancel the bond and thereafter shall be subject to a bond obligation only in accord with Sections 33.32 A. and D.
33.33 Apprentices:

A. In order to maintain a sufficient number of skilled mechanics, the necessity for employment of apprentices is hereby recognized, and the employment and proper training for as many apprentices as is reasonable and practicable shall be encouraged by all parties to this Agreement. To this end the Employers shall be required on the basis of a fair quota system established by the Trustees of the applicable Apprenticeship Program to employ as many apprentices as the Trustees of the Apprenticeship Program shall determine. Apprentices shall be under the complete control and jurisdiction of the Trustees of the Apprenticeship Program.
sections.subject: Firm

sections.content: B. Apprentice Training: The Apprenticeship Program shall train apprentices adequately in safety and first aid.
sections.subject: Firm

sections.content: C. Wages of Apprentices: The wages of apprentices shall be as follows:

50% of Journeyman's wage scale for 1st six months 60% of Journeyman's wage scale for 2nd six months 70% of Journeyman's wage scale for 3rd six months 80% of Journeyman's wage scale for 4th six months 90% of Journeyman's wage scale for 5th six months 95% of Journeyman's wage scale for 6th six months

D. Each Employer shall employ one (1) apprentice for each five (5) journeymen bricklayers when said apprentices are available, except that on all residential work three stories or less with a maximum of twenty-five dwelling units per structure, the Employer may, at his sole option, employ up to two apprentices for each journeyman bricklayer.
sections.subject: Firm

sections.content: E. In order to expose apprentices to all aspects of the trade, apprentices shall not operate a saw for more than
sections.subject: Worker

sections.content: eight (8) hours in any one work week except in unusual circumstances. No apprentice shall be entitled to any back pay or other monetary remedy for any violation of this provision, it being understood that this provision shall be enforced solely by a cease and desist remedy for any such violation.

F. An apprentice category designated "Novice Trainee" will exist, with such category ceasing to exist effective May 31, 2004, unless the Parties agree otherwise. Employers may employ novice trainees to perform work covered by Article X. Each novice trainee must pay a $25.00 registration fee to the applicable Local Union and must produce the receipt for such payment while working as a novice trainee, and no Employer shall permit an individual to work as a novice trainee unless and until that individual presents the registration fee receipt to the Employer. Employment of each novice trainee is limited to a 200 hour probationary period, after which period the Employer must decide whether the novice trainee will be retained, either as an advanced apprentice through the Local 21 apprenticeship program or as an apprentice through the apprenticeship program of Local 14, 20, 27, 56, or 74, or be terminated. No individual may work as a novice trainee for more than 200 hours for any one Employer or a cumulative total of more than 200 hours for more than one Employer; and it shall be the responsibility of each Employer hiring an individual as a novice trainee to assure compliance with this requirement. The Employer must notify the District Council in writing when a novice trainee is either terminated or retained, and must do so within 48 hours of informing the novice trainee. Failure by the Employer to provide such written notice or otherwise abide by the requirements of this Section 33.33 may be grounds for the Joint Arbitration Board to impose an appropriate remedy, including barring the Employer from future employment of novice trainees. If the novice trainee is to be retained, it will be his or her responsibility to apply to the apprenticeship program affiliated with the appropriate Local Union, and such application will be treated as would any application for entry into that apprenticeship program. The decision of the Employer to terminate a novice trainee during or at the end of the probationary period will be at the Employer's sole discretion and will not be subject to challenge through
sections.subject: Firm

sections.content: the procédures of Article XII.

Novice trainees will be paid 45% of the minimum wage rate set for journeymen. No benefit fund contributions or other payments except wages will be paid on behalf of a novice trainee unless he or she is retained after the 200 hour probationary period, at which point the Employer must pay Health and Welfare and Annuity contributions retroactively for the probationary period; and thereafter all contributions and payments will be made on a prospective basis. The Employer recognizes that novice trainees will not have received the safety and first aid training provided by the Apprenticeship Program, and must take proper steps to compensate for that lack of training.
sections.subject: Firm

sections.content: An Employer may employ one novice trainee for the first ten or fewer journeymen in its employ. After the Employer uses an initial novice trainee, the Employer must abide by the ten to one ratio and at least one apprentice must be included among the ten journeymen when available. The Local Union in whose area the work is being performed must approve application of the ratio for employment of more than one novice trainee. Employers may only employ novice trainees if they are current on all fringe benefit fund contributions, and no Employer may employ a novice trainee if there is a pending Joint Arbitration Board decision with which it has not complied.
sections.subject: Firm

sections.content: 33.34 Refractory Provisions:
All refractory provisions shall be superseded by the International Union Agreement when negotiated.
sections.subject: Union

sections.content: 33.35 Composite Crews:

For in-plant and precast installation work involving composite crews of Bricklayers and Boilermakers or IronWorkers, Bricklayer employees will be entitled to the most favorable show-up and premium pay provisions for such work.
sections.subject: Firm

sections.content: ARTICLE XXXIV SAVINGS CLAUSE 34.1

Should any of the terms and conditions of this Agreement be found in violation of any federal or state law, based on final court decisions or rulings of authorized governmental agencies, then such terms and conditions shall become void and ineffective immediately on written notice to this effect from one party to the other, but all other provisions of this Agreement shall continue in full force and effect.

In the event there is a disagreement on the legal interpretation of said court decisions or rulings, the subject matter shall be promptly referred to the Joint Arbitration Board for final determination through legal counsel.

category_summaries.summary: Recognition provisions include: the Agreement covers Cook, Lake, Will (except the DuPont Plant on the western edge of Grundy County), Grundy, DuPage, Kendall, DeKalb, Kane, and McHenry Counties, Illinois, and may be extended to additional territory later acquired by the Unions or the District Council with International Union approval. Employers covered only through the Builders Association of Chicago are bound only for work performed in Cook, Lake, and DuPage Counties. The District Council and local structures require associations to notify the District Council within 14 days of membership/assignment details, and employees’ “Home Local” is determined by the Local Union membership within the District Council; fringe contributions are directed to the Home Local affiliated funds (or, if no Home Local, to the Local within whose jurisdiction the work is performed), except that local apprenticeship/training contributions are always distributed through the Depository Account to the apprenticeship and training fund affiliated with the jurisdiction where the work is performed. The Union is recognized as the sole and exclusive bargaining representative for bricklayers and allied craftworkers/stone masons and apprentices regarding pay, wages, hours, and other conditions of employment, and for Health & Welfare and Pension/Annuity contribution purposes the bargaining unit also includes certain supervisors (as defined by the Labor-Management Relations Act) who were formerly employee members, unless written notice is given to the applicable trust funds within 30 days of becoming supervisors.

Management-related provisions provide that the Employer controls, at its sole discretion (and subject to Union approval for other devices), whether bricklayers may use mechanical mortar spreaders, caulking guns, and other approved tools with high-bond epoxy mortars. Bricklayers may perform extensive masonry installation and production-aid tasks (including preparation, drilling/cutting/fitting, fastening to steel frames/back-up panels by bolts/clips/pins and related welding, and full application of insulating/caulking/waterproofing, plus production/installation steps such as leveling/plumbing/anchoring, grouting/patching, and gasket/packing caulking), with composite crews allowed only if supervised by a bricklayer. Temporary frames/templates/falsework and similar aids may be used on all construction types at the Employer’s discretion, and installation of production aids must be done by bricklayers. Foremen requirements include: a foreman on jobs employing four or more bricklayers/stone masons (with sole authority to hire/discharge), permitting foreman tool-working up to and including jobs with twelve such workers (including the foreman), and requiring a non-working foreman for jobs exceeding twelve. Foremen must be skilled and competent and must keep complete records of jobs (notifying the Union at start and completion) and receive relevant plans. Foremen discipline authority is limited to legitimate and just reasons, and the bricklayer foreman is responsible for hiring and discharging bricklayers; additionally, there is no limit on the amount of work an employee may perform during working hours. Concrete block laying is within Union jurisdiction but does not limit bricklayers’ rights to perform the same work, and subcontracting of brick-laying/masonry work is restricted (except for specified categories such as stone work and certain hollow tile/caulking/cleaning/pointing, with exterior caulking to be subcontracted before exterior walls are completed to subcontractors employing bricklayers).

Compensation provisions require weekly wage payment by the contractor (payroll checks delivered to employees on the job) no later than 4:00 P.M. Wednesday following the workweek, except where a Monday holiday occurs in the payment week, in which case payment is due by 4:00 P.M. Thursday; payroll checks must display the contractor’s name, office/home address, and telephone number, and include an attached detachable stub itemizing Social Security and other authorized deductions. If inclement weather or lack of work prevents payday payment, the contractor must arrange for the check to be on the job by 11:00 A.M. On “Standard Payment,” wages and fringe benefit contributions are tied to Section 7.4, but the parties may via duly executed side letters negotiated by appointed District Council and Northern Illinois Mason Employers Council representatives vary fringe benefit contributions by Local Union; otherwise contributions follow the employee’s Home Local formula, or, if no Home Local, the Local Union jurisdiction where work is performed, with employees covered by a reciprocity agreement receiving the Standard Payment. Compensation increases of $1.60 per hour apply effective June 1, 2001, June 1, 2002, and June 1, 2003, with each increase allocated among wages and existing fringe benefit funds; Health & Welfare increases are limited to actuarially required amounts recommended unanimously by fund trustees, and International Pension Fund contributions cannot be increased without Northern Illinois Mason Employers Council consent. Job-specific wage differentials include: sewer/manhole/catch basin/conduit/tunnel pipe-sewer joint work paid at 25¢/hour over the regular rate; after the initial 75' on stack/chimney/refractory/refractory substitutes, an additional 10% rate for each succeeding 40'; smoke stack and tall chimney work paid 50¢/hour above the prevailing rate; underground work paid 25¢/hour above the applicable scale; compressed air work paid at not less than $2.00/hour over current scale (other “hazard” pay to be negotiated on-site before commencement). For wage advertising above scale, employers cannot reduce bricklayer/mason wages until job completion, and any above-scale wage offered becomes the prevailing wage for all covered employees on that job until completion (valid subsistence is excluded from “wages”); interior marble/polished stone masonry under the employer’s assignment to marble teams requires paying the marble mason gross rate less fringe contributions per this agreement. Foremen must receive at least $2.00/hour above the journeyman rate, and sub-foremen (if used) at least 50¢/hour over the journeyman rate with no hiring/discharge authority. Tool loss after quitting time when locked in the shed triggers $200.00 for tool loss and $50.00 for clothes loss due to fire or theft. Carbon work allows 20 minutes cleanup time at noon and quitting each day and pays 25¢/hour above the agreement rate. Double-time applies for fire brick and related work performed before 8:00 A.M. and after 4:30 P.M. Monday–Friday (unless modified by mutual written agreement) and for such work on Saturdays, Sundays, and holidays. Shift differentials are 12¢/hour (4:00 P.M.–12 midnight) and 16¢/hour (12 midnight–8:00 A.M.). For in-plant/precasing composite crews involving Bricklayers with Boilermakers/Ironworkers, Bricklayer employees receive the most favorable show-up and premium pay provisions for that work. The wage-and-contribution schedule also applies to contractors bargaining through the Will and Grundy Counties Contractors Association, with the same June 1, 2001–June 1, 2003 $1.60/hour increases and related Standard Payment periods (through May 31 of each following year).

The contract sets the work week for pay from 8:00 A.M. Monday to 8:00 A.M. the following Monday; with written mutual agreement between the Employer and Union, a job’s start may be advanced (not earlier than 7:00 A.M.) and quitting time must be 8½ hours after the start, but neither party is responsible for premium pay or obtaining/paying it if a bricklayer reports earlier than 7:00 A.M. Time checks made at the Employer’s office are valid if the employee is allowed up to two hours for travel time added to the time check; if the employee is not paid promptly and must wait during working hours, regular wages apply for waiting time, and if directed during the day to move between job sites, wages cover reasonable travel time between sites. The normal work week is 40 hours at the minimum wage rate; time-and-one-half applies for work beyond 40 hours in a week, beyond 8 hours in a day, or on Saturdays (with further rules: no discipline for refusing more than 8 hours/day or 40 hours/week or on a Saturday; Saturday make-up for inclement weather is straight time with crew preference, but a contractor proven to have worked a Saturday make-up for any reason other than inclement weather is ineligible for Saturday make-up for the rest of the term; holiday make-up Saturdays are double-time, and any Saturday hours over 8 are paid at double-time). Scheduling also includes tool-house timing rules (including potential adjustments when start time advances to 7:00 A.M.), mandatory breaks (10-minute morning break no earlier than 2 hours and no later than 3 hours after start), and lunch rules (generally a flexible 30-minute lunch between 12:00 Noon and 1:30 P.M., except refractory-fire brick workers; if a 12+ hour shift is approved, an additional 30-minute lunch is added at Employer expense after 8 hours and every 4 hours thereafter; and when multiple shifts are worked, the lunch period is included in paid working time). Work is prohibited on Sundays and six named holidays (New Year’s, Memorial Day, Fourth of July, Labor Day, Thanksgiving, Christmas) unless the Union permits it, in which case double-time applies; Labor Day work requires dire emergency and the President of the Union’s consent. If a non-holiday day is missed during a holiday week due to inclement weather, Saturday may be scheduled as a straight-time make-up; otherwise, Saturday work during a holiday week is double-time, with specific double-time/regular-rate treatment for Saturdays before versus after Labor Day or Memorial Day. Additional scheduling/availability provisions include presumptive payment based on hours between starting and quitting times as determined by Local Union representatives, inclement-weather rotation efforts, interior work substitution when exterior work is prevented (and continued interior placement if possible), a rule limiting bricklayers on bottom block (one course at a time), a fire-brick cleaning-up/walking-time accommodation, special shift pay mechanics (second/third shifts paid as 8 hours for 7½ hours worked at the regular rate; no one works more than one shift unless others fail to report, excluding cupola lining/retort/conduit work), a two-hours’ pay for lost time when ordered to report and not put to work except for specified causes, and an obligation for employees not intending to report at 8:00 A.M. (or 7:00 A.M. by written mutual agreement) to notify the Employer, with failure to report/notify subject to discipline.

For Healthcare (Health and Welfare) benefits, the parties may allocate fringe benefit fund contributions based on the employee’s Local Union affiliation or the location where work is performed, with contributions directed to the appropriate Health and Welfare Fund specified in the applicable wage provisions and made in accordance with the Fund’s Agreement/Declaration of Trust. Employers must contribute the specified per-hour Health and Welfare amount for all covered employees and supervisors, and payments must be received by the bank on or before the 20th day of each month for work performed during the prior month. Late or nonpayment triggers monthly liquidated damages equal to 1% per month on all unpaid amounts (including liquidated damages), recognizing the difficulty of calculating damages from late payment. If employees are withdrawn from a job to collect contributions, affected employees are paid for lost time up to 16 hours, provided the Union gives the Employer at least two (2) days’ notice of the intention to remove employees by registered or certified mail. Contributions generally accrue for all hours worked by covered journeymen/apprentices or supervisors to the extent this Agreement provides, and there is no double contribution where work is performed outside the Local’s jurisdiction under another effective Welfare/Pension plan to which the employer contributes; however, the primary duty is to contribute under this Agreement for work performed within the Local’s jurisdiction.

The parties agree to create jointly administered successor trust arrangements for the industry promotion and advancement funds (excluding the Masonry Industry Advancement Fund ("MIAF")), addressing their dispute under Section 302(c) of the Taft-Hartley Act by limiting employee-representative trusteeship; contributions under the contract that would otherwise be payable to the Illinois Masonry Institute and the applicable local funds are payable instead to the successor trusts. If the jointly administered funds (other than MIAF) are not implemented within 30 days after a final federal court judgment as described, then contract contributions to the Illinois Masonry Institute and local industry promotion/advancement funds cease 30 days after the Union gives notice of termination to the Council. In addition, the Employer must make specified per-hour contributions for all covered employees and supervisors to the relevant trust funds: pension contributions to the applicable Pension Fund; promotion/training contributions to the International Masonry Institute Promotion Trust and the appropriate Local Promotion Trust (including a trustee composition of five Trustees for the Illinois Masonry Institute Promotion Trust—three appointed by the Mason Contractors Association of Greater Chicago and two by the Builders Association of Chicago—with the Trustees advised by five Union-appointed persons); contributions to the Masonry Industry Advancement Fund per the wage provisions; and annuity contributions to the appropriate Annuity Fund, explicitly including the premium rates contained in the paid wages so weekly annuity contributions track the equivalent of straight time plus time-and-a-half hours (e.g., 40 straight + 4 time-and-a-half equals 46 hours for annuity contribution purposes). The Employer also agrees to be bound by the Trust Agreements/Declarations and Trustee actions, and the Union will cooperate to ensure required contributions are made; delayed payment/delinquency triggers liability for the value of benefits that would have been owed plus contributions, liquidated damages, and reasonable legal fees for multiple covered funds (including Promotion Trust Funds and the International Pension Fund). Employers must also provide annual information to the various trust fund trustees (corporate officers/directors or other constituent persons) and monthly remittance reporting to the Bricklayers Northern Trust Fringe Benefit Account listing employees.

Security-related provisions include: (1) job staffing priority—on all jobs, the Employer must give first priority to qualified employees with prior experience with Employers covered by the Agreement, and second priority to qualified employees who previously worked in the industry within the Local Union jurisdiction where the job is located; in any event, at least fifty (50) percent of employees on each job within a Local Union’s jurisdiction must meet both of these criteria. (2) layoff handling—employees who are laid off are entitled, upon demand, to pay on the next regular pay day (except for layoffs caused by bad weather or unusually high joists), and any laid-off employee must be given one half hour to gather tools; additionally, for layoffs due to lack of material, the laid-off bricklayers must be given first chance to return to work, with enforcement obligation on the steward and business agent. (3) security instrument/bond substitution—the Union may, at its sole discretion, accept a cash bond, irrevocable letter of credit, or other acceptable security instrument, and references to a “bond” throughout the Agreement are deemed to include such alternate instruments.

Training provisions require that work involving foundations and masonry walls be performed under the supervision of a qualified bricklayer or mason, and that apprentices and qualified tradespeople be used consistently with apprenticeship rules (successful completion of the apprenticeship program qualifies the worker; others must pass a qualification exam, and the Employer gives first consideration to qualified, experienced workers covered by the Agreement). The Employer must contribute, in addition to wages, for apprenticeship and training purposes the amounts specified in the wage provisions of the Agreement—paid to the named Apprenticeship and Training Program Trustees (including the International Masonry Apprenticeship Trust) and also separately the District Council Training Center Fund—on an hourly basis for each covered employee. Apprenticeship employment is encouraged to maintain skilled mechanics, with Employers required to meet a fair quota system set by the Trustees, and apprentices under the Trustees’ complete control; the program must provide adequate safety and first aid training, and apprentices are restricted from operating a saw for more than the stated (unspecified) amount of time. A “Novice Trainee” category may be used (existing only until May 31, 2004 unless extended by agreement) subject to a $25.00 local registration fee and proof to the Employer, a 200-hour maximum probationary period per trainee per Employer (and no more than 200 hours cumulatively across Employers), and mandatory written notice to the District Council within 48 hours of termination or retention (noncompliance may trigger a Joint Arbitration Board remedy, including barring future novice-trainee employment). Novice trainees are paid 45% of the journeyman minimum wage, receive no benefit contributions during probation unless retained (then Health and Welfare and Annuity are paid retroactively for the probationary period and thereafter prospectively), and Employers must address the lack of safety/first-aid training. Employers may employ novice trainees at a one-per-ten-jounreymen ratio (with at least one apprentice included when available), must obtain Local Union area approval for employing more than one novice trainee, and may only employ novice trainees if current on all fringe benefit contributions and not subject to any pending Joint Arbitration Board decision with which they have not complied.

For disputes, the Employer must notify the Union by 4:00 P.M. on the preceding Friday when employees are to perform Saturday work, including the Employer’s name/location and the job site; if the Employer fails to provide such notice, the Union may demand an immediate audit of the Employer’s records at the Employer’s expense. Disputes that cannot be resolved between the Employer and the Union are referred to the Joint Arbitration Board (JAB), and grievances must be filed within ninety (90) days of the occurrence or when the party reasonably should have known; late grievances are waived. The JAB has four (4) appointees from the District Council and four (4) from the Associations, with quorum of two (2) from each side and decisions requiring majority vote and being binding; management appointees must be eligible mason contractors contributing to funds and signatory to a District Council CBA, and Union appointees must be members of District Council locals. Arbitration is administered per the American Arbitration Association (AAA): the requesting party selects the arbitrator per AAA procedures, an arbitrator is designated if no agreement within one (1) week after a panel is tendered, the arbitrator issues a decision without written opinion within 48 hours after submission unless otherwise agreed, and the award is final and binding; arbitration costs are split equally between the contractor and Union (except legal counsel). During conciliation/arbitration, pre-dispute working conditions are not changed, and the JAB/arbitrator may impose appropriate enforcement remedies. Where an Employer is required to post a payment bond and fails to do so within ten (10) days after a written request, the Union may seek immediate court relief without using the grievance/arbitration procedure and may recover reasonable legal fees and costs; separately, the JAB may order a payment bond (even without a current delinquency) if it finds a reasonable possibility wages/contributions/dues will be lost absent action, requiring compliance within ten (10) days of written notice or allowing the Union to use the immediate-court/fee-shifting procedures.

The Agreement emphasizes strict compliance with all applicable state and federal safety laws and prevailing safety regulations, including on union- jurisdiction scaffolding, and requires Local Unions to take reasonable steps to ensure compliance by employers and employees. Employers must carry required Workers’ Compensation insurance (and employees may not work for uninsured employers), provide safety equipment when required (e.g., hard hats with new liner/sweatbands; cover/replace costs for lost or damaged issued equipment), and provide jobsite facilities and protections such as suitable exclusive-use shanties for multi-story/masonry work (location, gang boxes every four floors, lighting/heating from Oct. 15–Apr. 15, keys/ventilation, and tool/work-clothing loss responsibility), suitable overhead covering, toilets or time to reach public toilets, and clean drinking water (with different requirements for Local 14 and options for iced water between May 1–Sep. 1). Safety-related pay/benefits include a $1.00 per hour over the Agreement’s minimum wage for bricklayers working in monitored atomic radiation areas or where radioactive materials are present, and double-time for all “Hot Work” (defined by operations/temperatures above those present after cooling, including specific hot equipment locations). Safety duties include having foremen and stewards act as safety men with authority to declare jobs unsafe (and steward access to the shed/key and work rules), accompanying safety inspectors by a bricklayer foreman/designee (with pay), and injury response/notification by steward and foreman. Operational safety provisions include requirements for PPE and controls for dusty or hazardous work (masks/goggles for dry cutting; gloves/apron/platform for wet cutting; dust-extraction and grounding for dry cutting machines; respirators/goggles, dust wet-down where possible, and additional precautions for gas and excessive hot work, including counter-fatigue aids, gloves/protective materials, wooden shoes for heated surfaces, and employer responsibility for burned/damaged tools/shoes/clothes), fire extinguisher availability on scaffolds for certain fire-brick jobs, safety glasses for high-temperature cement work above blast furnace mantels, and prohibitions such as no rack permitted in a blast furnace and no non-approved tools/material placement practices. Site/means-and-methods requirements cover ladder provision, scaffold limits (generally not over five feet high absent obstruction), scaffold width and wall/material spacing, mortar board elevation, team placement rules for block units (two workers for blocks weighing 35 pounds or more), and specific masonry layout duties for coke oven walls (saddling/raising line simultaneously by two bricklayers). Physical examination is not required as a hiring condition, and discrimination protections apply.

During the term of the Agreement, refractory provisions are to be superseded by the International Union Refractory Agreement once negotiated; however, if an Employer is a party to both agreements, the Union will allow refractory work to be performed under either agreement at the Employer’s option. The parties agree not to order, maintain, sanction, or engage in strikes, lockouts, stoppages of work, or boycotts affecting the other party except as expressly provided in the Agreement. Employers’ liability for breaches is several (not joint), limited to each Employer’s own acts; similarly, the District Council/Local Unions are several, and Unions’ liability is limited to their role as negotiating agents without liability for individual members. The Union has broad enforcement rights for nonpayment and delinquency: employees who do not receive wages on pay day must immediately report to the Union; the Union may stop work and require that employees not be asked to work again until all wages and fringe benefits are paid, with employees then permitted to return without discrimination or reprisal. For failure to make required payroll/fringe/promotion fund contributions records available, the Union may stop jobs and publicize such stoppages, and affected employees must be paid for lost time up to 16 hours if the Union gives two days’ notice to the Employer by specified methods. The Agreement also requires (including where owner-approved) masonry/brick-layer contractors to display identifying signage, restricts donated work to immediate family or another member (with Union notice), prohibits employees from soliciting subscriptions for gifts/donations to foremen or superintendents, and requires prior arrangements for Union representatives to enter secured job sites. Finally, the Agreement contains committee, inspection, reporting, auditing, and bond-related administration for wage/fringe compliance and contribution obligations, including jobsite visitation, audit cost shifting based on violation findings, periodic compliance meetings (on or about the 15th day of each calendar quarter), and employer bonding requirements triggered by delinquencies and bond-posting failures, with timeframes ranging from 10 days to 72 hours and ongoing bond maintenance until obligations are satisfied and no delinquencies occur for two years.
